related_questions.question: How soon after being exposed to COVID do you get it?
related_questions.snippet: Key points. People with COVID-19 have a wide range of symptoms ranging from mild symptoms to severe illness. Symptoms may appear 2-14 days after exposure to the virus. Symptoms may start as mild, and some people will progress to more severe symptoms.
related_questions.title: Symptoms of COVID-19 - CDC

related_questions.question: What should I do if I was exposed to someone with COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: If you've been exposed to someone with COVID-19, you should immediately start taking precautions, including wearing a high-quality mask. You should also monitor for symptoms and get tested at least 5 days after your last exposure, even if you don't feel sick. If you develop symptoms, isolate immediately and get tested.
snippet_highlighted_words: immediately start taking precautions, including wearing a high-quality mask

list.title: Immediately start precautions:
list.snippet: Begin wearing a high-quality mask, like an N95 or KN95, as soon as you find out about the exposure.

list.title: Monitor for symptoms:
list.snippet: Pay close attention to potential COVID-19 symptoms such as fever, cough, shortness of breath, and others.

list.title: Get tested:
list.snippet: Regardless of whether you have symptoms, test at least 5 full days after your last exposure, according to the CDC.

list.title: Isolate if symptomatic:
list.snippet: If you develop any symptoms, isolate immediately and get tested.

list.title: Continue precautions:
list.snippet: Even with a negative test, continue taking precautions for a full 10 days after your last exposure.

related_questions.question: What if you were exposed to COVID but tested negative?

text_blocks.snippet: A negative COVID-19 test result, especially with an antigen test, doesn't definitively rule out infection. If you've been exposed and have symptoms, it's possible you could have COVID-19 but the virus wasn't detectable yet during the initial test. Following FDA recommendations for repeat testing with antigen tests is advised, according to the CDC. If you used a PCR test and it's negative, you're likely not contagious, but this might depend on the timing of the test in relation to symptom onset.
